medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Pharmacy call - new prescription
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacist called: new rx for propranolol 20 mg BID from his GI doctor, filled yesterday; wanted to confirm we were aware given amlodipine on profile. We had not received anything from GI yet. Pt confirms by phone that GI did a scope on the 8th, found "small veins" in the esophagus, and started the pill. Added to med list as outside med. GI note requested. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep A dose 2 (series complete) L deltoid, hep B dose 3 (series complete) R deltoid. One week into propranolol, feels a little more tired in the afternoons, no lightheadedness. BP and pulse recorded. Updated vaccine record printed for pt.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and upper endoscopy (visit 2024-01-08)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CLINIC LETTER
Date of service: 01/08/2024
Referred by: primary care, for alcohol-related cirrhosis with ascites

Thank you for sending Mr. Pomeroy, 53, whose cirrhosis came to light last summer when he presented with a distended abdomen. He tells me he has been abstinent for roughly six months and is attending an outpatient recovery program. He also gave up cigarettes in July. He has no complaints today aside from an intermittent mild burning in the upper abdomen that he calls indigestion. No melena, hematemesis or confusion.

PMH: hypertension; remote peptic ulcer; alcohol use disorder; cirrhosis with ascites, controlled on diuretics.
Meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father died at 58 of alcohol-related cirrhosis.

Exam: BP 140/90, HR 78, afebrile. No jaundice. Abdomen soft without ascites; spleen tip palpable, moderately enlarged; liver edge firm and palpable below the costal margin. No peripheral edema. No asterixis.

Labs today: platelets 110, AST 70, ALT 50, total bilirubin 1.2, albumin 3.9, INR 1.1.

Procedure (same day): Diagnostic esophagogastroduodenoscopy under moderate sedation. Small esophageal varices in the distal esophagus. No red wale markings. No stigmata of recent bleeding. Stomach and duodenum without ulcer.

Impression: Compensated-on-treatment alcoholic cirrhosis with portal hypertension; small esophageal varices meeting our threshold for primary prophylaxis.

Plan:
1. Start propranolol 20 mg twice daily; hold for pulse under 55 or dizziness.
2. Continue current diuretics and pantoprazole.
3. Liver ultrasound every 6 months for surveillance; we would appreciate the PCP ordering these locally.
4. Repeat endoscopy in about a year, sooner for any bleeding.
5. Total abstinence; he is doing very well.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cirrhosis f/u. GI letter (1/8 visit) finally reached us in February - reviewed: small varices on scope, no red signs, propranolol 20 BID started; ultrasound q6 months asked of us.

Now ~10.5 months without alcohol, still in recovery group weekly. No smoking. Tolerating propranolol; a bit less stamina climbing stairs, otherwise fine. No bleeding, no dark stools, no confusion. Belly stays flat on the diuretics. The indigestion GI mentioned comes and goes, mild, no change in pattern.

Meds reconciled: amlodipine 5, pantoprazole 40, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, propranolol 20 BID.

Exam: BP 126/80, HR 64. Wt 78. Anicteric. Spider angiomas on the chest. Abdomen soft, no shifting dullness, spleen tip felt. No edema. No asterixis.

A/P
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis with portal HTN - stable, ascites controlled. Labs today.
2. Esophageal varices on primary prophylaxis - HR at a sensible target.
3. AUD, early remission - continuing.
4. HCC surveillance US ordered for July.
5. Peptic ulcer history - on pantoprazole.

RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: April labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look steady: bilirubin 1.3, albumin 3.8, clotting normal, liver enzymes still drifting down. Platelets 105, about where they have been. Nothing to change. Ultrasound in July.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN, LIVER SURVEILLANCE
Indication: Cirrhosis; hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance.
Comparison: 06/29/2023.
Liver: Nodular contour and coarse echotexture as before. No focal hepatic mass.
Portal vein: Patent, hepatopetal flow.
Gallbladder: Normal, no stones.
Bile ducts: Not dilated.
Spleen: Enlarged, 14.6 cm.
Kidneys: Unremarkable.
Ascites: None.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver without focal lesion. Splenomegaly. No ascites. Continue surveillance in 6 months.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Surveillance US: no liver mass, no fluid. Repeat in January. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Wife calling - patient hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. He was admitted to a regional hospital yesterday: for a few days he was mixing up words, sleeping in the daytime, and his belly was swelling up again. She says he had started drinking again sometime in August, mostly at night. Hospital told her it is "ammonia from the liver." Asked her to have the hospital send the discharge summary here; gave our fax. Post-discharge visit to be booked once she knows the discharge date. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (admitted 2024-09-10, discharged 2024-09-14)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 09/10/2024   Discharge: 09/14/2024
Service: Hospital Medicine

Principal diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy.
Secondary: Alcoholic cirrhosis with recurrent ascites; portal hypertension; esophageal varices on beta-blocker; alcohol use disorder with recent relapse; hypertension.

History: 53-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis brought by his wife after several days of daytime somnolence, word-finding trouble and increasing abdominal girth. Resumed drinking about a month before admission after roughly 14 months of abstinence.

Course: On arrival drowsy but arousable, with asterixis and ascites. Infectious evaluation unrevealing. No GI bleeding. Started on lactulose with rapid improvement; mental status at baseline by hospital day 3. Diuretics continued. Alcohol withdrawal monitored without significant symptoms. Social work met with patient and wife regarding return to outpatient treatment.

Discharge medications:
- Lactulose 30 mL by mouth twice daily, adjust to 2-3 soft bowel movements a day (NEW)
- Spironolactone 100 mg daily
- Furosemide 40 mg daily
- Propranolol 20 mg twice daily
- Pantoprazole 40 mg daily
- Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; gastroenterology as scheduled. No driving until cleared. Abstain from alcohol.

medications.sig: Take 30 mL by mouth twice daily; adjust to 2-3 soft bowel movements daily

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, discharged 9/14. Summary received 9/20 and reviewed. Wife with him; RN reached them by phone 9/16 for the interactive contact.

Admitted 9/10-9/14 for hepatic encephalopathy with fluid back in the belly; infection workup negative; cleared quickly on lactulose.

Now: thinking clear per wife. On lactulose 30 mL twice a day, getting 2-3 soft BMs; she watches the count. Belly a bit fuller than spring. No bleeding.

Alcohol: honest about it - started again in August, a few beers most nights, more on weekends. Has had nothing since admission. Wants to go back to the program; already called them. AUDIT-C scored for the past year: 8.
Mood: down about the relapse, PHQ-9 6, no SI.

Meds reconciled; lactulose added to our list.

Exam: BP 124/78. Wt 80 (78 in April). Awake, oriented x3, conversant. No asterixis. Anicteric. Abdomen mildly distended with shifting dullness, nontender. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
1. Hepatic encephalopathy, first episode - resolved on lactulose. Continue; titrate to 2-3 BMs. No driving for now.
2. Ascites, recurrent with the relapse - same diuretics, strict low salt; weigh daily.
3. AUD with relapse - re-entering outpatient program. Talked about his father without lecturing. He knows.
4. Varices - propranolol continues; GI recheck scope is due around the new year.
5. Flu shot offered - he declined today, "too much going on."

Labs today. RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner if any confusion.

documents.title: Post-hospital labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Scott and Linda - labs from yesterday: bilirubin is back up to 2.4, albumin down to 3.1, liver enzymes higher (AST 110), sodium slightly low at 133, platelets 92. Kidney function is fine. This is the liver reacting to the drinking this summer, and much of it can improve again with sobriety, like last year. No medication changes. Please keep the salt low and the fluids reasonable.
